title: USP11 regulates proliferation and apoptosis of human spermatogonial stem cells via HOXC5-mediated canonical WNT/beta-catenin signaling pathway.
authors: Gao, Jun; Xu, Zhipeng; Song, Weijie; Huang, Jiwei; Liu, Wei; He, Zuping; He, Leye
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
one_liner_zh: 研究USP11通过HOXC5/WNT通路调控精原干细胞增殖凋亡，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Spermatogonial stem cells (SSCs) are capable of transmitting genetic information to the next generations and they are the initial cells for spermatogenesis. Nevertheless, it remains largely unknown about key genes and signaling pathways that regulate fate determinations of human SSCs and male infertility. In this study, we explored the expression, function, and mechanism of USP11 in controlling the proliferation and apoptosis of human SSCs as well as the association between its abnormality and azoospermia. We found that USP11 was predominantly expressed in human SSCs as shown by database analysis and immunohistochemistry. USP11 silencing led to decreases in proliferation and DNA synthesis and an enhancement in apoptosis of human SSCs. RNA-sequencing identified HOXC5 as a target of USP11 in human SSCs. Double immunofluorescence, Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and molecular docking demonstrated an interaction between USP11 and HOXC5 in human SSCs. HOXC5 knockdown suppressed the growth of human SSCs and increased apoptosis via the classical WNT/beta-catenin pathway. In contrast, HOXC5 overexpression reversed the effect of proliferation and apoptosis induced by USP11 silencing. Significantly, lower levels of USP11 expression were observed in the testicular tissues of patients with spermatogenic disorders. Collectively, these results implicate that USP11 regulates the fate decisions of human SSCs through the HOXC5/WNT/beta-catenin pathway. This study thus provides novel insights into understanding molecular mechanisms underlying human spermatogenesis and the etiology of azoospermia and it offers new targets for gene therapy of male infertility.
abstract_zh: 精原干细胞（SSCs）能够将遗传信息传递给下一代，是精子发生的起始细胞。然而，调控人类精原干细胞命运决定及男性不育的关键基因和信号通路仍 largely 未知。在本研究中，我们探讨了USP11在调控人类精原干细胞增殖与凋亡中的表达、功能及机制，并分析了其异常与无精子症之间的关联。通过数据库分析和免疫组织化学，我们发现USP11主要表达于人类精原干细胞中。USP11沉默导致人类精原干细胞增殖和DNA合成减少，凋亡增强。RNA测序鉴定出HOXC5为USP11在人类精原干细胞中的靶标。双重免疫荧光、共免疫沉淀（Co-IP）和分子对接实验证明USP11与HOXC5在人类精原干细胞中存在相互作用。HOXC5敲低通过经典WNT/β-catenin通路抑制人类精原干细胞生长并增加凋亡。相反，HOXC5过表达逆转了USP11沉默诱导的增殖和凋亡效应。值得注意的是，在生精障碍患者的睾丸组织中观察到USP11表达水平较低。综合这些结果，提示USP11通过HOXC5/WNT/β-catenin通路调控人类精原干细胞的命运决定。因此，本研究为理解人类精子发生的分子机制及无精子症的病因提供了新见解，并为男性不育的基因治疗提供了新靶点。
